item.title: US says ambassador’s comments on Israel and the Middle East were taken out of context
item.description: An uproar continued Sunday after the U.S. ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, said Israel has a right to much of the Middle East, as more Arab and Muslim countries objected and the U.S. said his comments were taken out of context.

item.title: Display of St. Francis of Assisi’s bones confirms enduring appeal of relics for Christians
item.description: The bones of St. Francis of Assisi went on public display for the first time Sunday, capping an 800-year saga over his bodily remains and confirming the enduring appeal to Christians of venerating a saint’s relics.

item.title: Photos from Assisi as the bones of St. Francis go on display
item.description: Pilgrims will have yet another reason to visit the hilltop Umbrian town of Assisi, as the bones of St. Francis of Assisi, the medieval friar who inspired Pope Francis and generations of Christians before him, go on public display for the first time.

item.title: 82-year-old nun killed in Brazilian convent
item.description: An 82-year-old nun was brutally killed in Brazil by an unknown man who invaded the convent where she lived.

item.title: Supporters of jailed Ugandan opposition figure pray for him after president tries to stop it
item.description: Hundreds of supporters of detained Ugandan opposition figure Kizza Besigye held a defiant prayer service inside a Catholic cathedral on Monday to press authorities to free him after more than a year without trial on treason charges, saying he is in failing health.

item.title: Church gains prominence in humanitarian work in Cuba as criticism of the regime intensifies
item.description: As Cuba faces its worst social crisis in decades, the Catholic Church has taken on the role of a central provider of humanitarian assistance on the island.

item.title: Milan church concert strikes a chord for inclusion ahead of Winter Paralympics
item.description: Days ahead of the Winter Paralympics, when disabled athletes will take center stage at the Milan Cortina Games, a choir from northern Italy performed a pop music concert inside Milan’s Sant’Antonio church.

item.title: ‘Flour war’ erupts in Greek seaside town as revelers celebrate the start of Lent
item.description: The Greek seaside town of Galaxidi exploded into a messy and colorful “flour war” on Monday for its annual end of carnival season festivities that mark the start of the Lent season.

item.title: India’s Supreme Court grants temporary relief to tribal Christians in burial dispute
item.description: A three-judge panel of India’s Supreme Court issued a temporary ruling on February 18 restraining the forcible exhumation and relocation of the bodies of tribal Christians from their village burial grounds in Chhattisgarh state.

item.title: On anniversary of Russian invasion, Major Archbishop says Pope Leo understands Ukraine
item.description: The leader of the Catholic Church in the embattled nation says Pope Leo XIV sees the conflict in a “European context.”
